answer: Divergent challenge ledger: each identity gets a challenge chain seeded by a hidden marble drawn once at registration. To transact, an identity must extend its chain with a fresh response within a time window, and counterparties verify the tail. Clones inheriting one seed produce identical chains, so a split is detectable the moment two responses diverge on the same slot. An attacker must run one full independent chain per puppet, each requiring its own ferrous hardware token and continuous compute, making N clones cost N times the single identity anchor overhead rather than a shared copy.
